To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DNA synthesis in African Green Monkey (AGM) kidney cells infected with a defective simian virus (SV40) can occur in resting cells and that this synthesis can be stimulated by the addition of serum to the growth medium.
the DNA synthesis in resting African Green Monkey Kidney Cells infected with Defective Simian Virus 40 is not inhibited by the presence of a non-permissive host cell.

DNA synthesis in African green monkey kidney (AGMK) cells infected with a temperature-sensitive (ts) mutant of SV 40 (SV 40 ts A) was not affected by the ts mutation, and the DNA synthesized in these infected cells was not detectable by the techniques used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the synthesis of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) in resting African green (AG) monkey kidney cells infected by a temperature-sensitive mutant of the Simian Virus 40, SV 40tsA58.
the study of DNA synthesis in SV 40-infected African green monkey kidney (AGMK) cells.
the study of DNA synthesis in resting monkey kidney cells (CV-1) infected with SV40.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA of the SV 40 virus is a double-stranded DNA molecule of 5,200 base pairs, with the two complementary strands coiled around each other in a right-handed helical form.
, although the DNA of the SV 40 genome was synthesized in the infected monkey kidney cells, it was not incorporated in the cellular DNA.

, although DNA synthesis in African green monkey kidney (AGMK) cells infected with defective simian virus 40 (SV 40) is stimulated, this effect is not due to an increase in the number of replicating cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA replication in the African green monkey kidney (AGMK) cells is a very complex process and the DNA synthesis is regulated by many factors.
we have shown that DNA synthesis in resting African Green Monkey Kidney cells infected with defective Simian virus 40 is inhibited by actinomycin D and cycloheximide.
the DNA synthesis in resting monkey kidney cells infected by a defective SV40 virus is inhibited by the virus, but the inhibition is not due to a block in the DNA synthesis itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SV 40 DNA replication origin is not essential for the replication of the virus, but is essential for the maintenance of the viral genome.
DNA synthesis is a very important part of the process of infection.
DNA replication in resting cells is possible.
